findings.where: "Where we're starting" section: the three destination cards (Canggu, Uluwatu, Kuta Lombok), at desktop and phone widths
findings.fault: The cards have a thick bright purple border. Purple is not in the palette and has no job in it. The rules file gives cards a thin sand-border edge. These are the brightest edges on the page, so they compete with the coral CTA and pull the page away from its turquoise, sand and ink colours.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who settled the brand sheet so that each colour has one job and turquoise and sand are the brand's colours. A backpacker sees a colour that appears nowhere else in Manta's identity, so the cards look like they belong to another site or a template.

findings.where: "Where we're starting" section: the three destination cards, at desktop and phone widths
findings.fault: The cards sit at rest under a large, soft, heavy shadow. The rules file says nothing rests under a heavy shadow: borders do the work, and shadows are for hover and popovers only. The parts map also shows the cards are static, so the shadow tells the visitor they can act on something that does nothing.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker who taps a card that looks raised and clickable and gets no response. Also the founder, whose elevation rule (borders first, shadow only for hover and popovers) these cards break.

findings.where: Destination cards: the "Best hostels" line with its chevron, on each card
findings.fault: The line is set in lagoon-text with a chevron. The rules file reserves that colour for links, but the parts map shows these lines are static, so the colour promises a link that is not there.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who taps "Best hostels" expecting the destination guide the page promises and nothing happens. The founder, because lagoon-text is meant only for links.

findings.where: Hero: the coral "Email … for launch news" button and the outline "Explore destinations" button below it, at desktop and phone widths
findings.fault: The two hero buttons have different corners, and neither matches the brand. The coral CTA is a full pill instead of the 8 px control radius. The outline button has square corners instead of 8 px. Two buttons stacked together therefore look like they come from different design systems.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose rules set one control radius (8 px) for buttons and keep capsules for badges and status chips. A careful visitor notices the mismatched pair at the most visible spot on the page, and it reads as unfinished.
